title: jsPsych Studio experiment spec
description: A declarative experiment the Studio compiler turns into jsPsych source. Edit it here or open it in the builder at https://www.capro.dev/jspsych-studio/.

$schema.title: This schema, so an editor knows how to check the file.

authors.title: Whoever made the experiment, in the shape Psych-DS expects for a person.

identifier.title: A URL that identifies them across datasets, usually an ORCID.

assets.title: Files the experiment shows, carried in the spec so it stays self-contained.

conditions.title: Conditions tables, each a list of rows a block can run over.

timeline.title: The steps of the experiment, in order.

trial.title: One step the participant sees, run by a jsPsych plugin.

plugin.title: The jsPsych plugin that runs this step.

tag.title: A label other steps can refer to, such as a loop judging these trials' accuracy.

record.title: Extra columns written to the data file for this trial.

stimulus.title: stimulus
stimulus.description: The audio file to be played.

choices.title: choices
choices.description: This array contains the key(s) that the participant is allowed to press in order to respond to the stimulus. Keys should be specified as characters (e.g., `'a'`, `'q'`, `' '`, `'Enter'`, `'ArrowDown'`) - see [this page](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/KeyboardEvent/key/Key_Values) and [this page (event.key column)](https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/javascript-keycode-list-keypress-event-key-codes/) for more examples. Any key presses that are not listed in the array will be ignored. The default value of `"ALL_KEYS"` means that all keys will be accepted as valid responses. Specifying `"NO_KEYS"` will mean that no responses are allowed.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.description: This string can contain HTML markup. Any content here will be displayed below the stimulus. The intention is that it can be used to provide a reminder about the action the participant is supposed to take (e.g., which key to press).

trial_duration.title: trial duration
trial_duration.description: How long to wait for the participant to make a response before ending the trial in milliseconds. If the participant fails to make a response before this timer is reached, the participant's response will be recorded as null for the trial and the trial will end. If the value of this parameter is null, then the trial will wait for a response indefinitely.

response_ends_trial.title: response ends trial
response_ends_trial.description: If true, then the trial will end whenever the participant makes a response (assuming they make their response before the cutoff specified by the `trial_duration` parameter). If false, then the trial will continue until the value for `trial_duration` is reached. You can use set this parameter to `false` to force the participant to listen to the stimulus for a fixed amount of time, even if they respond before the time is complete

trial_ends_after_audio.title: Trial ends after audio
trial_ends_after_audio.description: If true, then the trial will end as soon as the audio file finishes playing.

response_allowed_while_playing.title: response allowed while playing
response_allowed_while_playing.description: If true, then responses are allowed while the audio is playing. If false, then the audio must finish playing before a keyboard response is accepted. Once the audio has played all the way through, a valid keyboard response is allowed (including while the audio is being re-played via on-screen playback controls).

wait_for_key_release.title: wait for key release
wait_for_key_release.description: If true, the response is not registered until the participant releases the key. The response time (`rt`) still reflects when the key was pressed, and the additional data field `rt_key_duration` records how long the key was held down. Note that when this is true, the trial cannot end until the key is released: with `response_ends_trial: true` the trial ends at the key release, and if the trial ends for another reason (e.g., `trial_duration`) while the key is still held, no response is recorded for the trial.

async.title: async
async.description: Set to true if `func` is an asynchoronous function. If this is true, then the first argument passed to `func` will be a callback that you should call when the async operation is complete. You can pass data to the callback. See example below.

fullscreen_mode.title: fullscreen mode
fullscreen_mode.description: A value of `true` causes the experiment to enter fullscreen mode. A value of `false` causes the browser to exit fullscreen mode.

message.title: message
message.description:
`

The experiment will switch to full screen mode when you press the button below

` | The HTML content to display above the button to enter fullscreen mode.
message.default: The experiment will switch to full screen mode when you press the button below

button_label.title: button label
button_label.description: The text that appears on the button to enter fullscreen mode.

delay_after.title: delay after
delay_after.description: The length of time to delay after entering fullscreen mode before ending the trial. This can be useful because entering fullscreen is jarring and most browsers display some kind of message that the browser has entered fullscreen mode.

stimulus.title: stimulus
stimulus.description: The HTML content to be displayed.

choices.title: choices
choices.description: Labels for the buttons. Each different string in the array will generate a different button.

button_html.title: button html
button_html.description: A function that generates the HTML for each button in the `choices` array. The function gets the string and index of the item in the `choices` array and should return valid HTML. If you want to use different markup for each button, you can do that by using a conditional on either parameter. The default parameter returns a button element with the text label of the choice.

prompt.title: prompt
prompt.description: This string can contain HTML markup. Any content here will be displayed below the stimulus. The intention is that it can be used to provide a reminder about the action the participant is supposed to take (e.g., which key to press).

stimulus_duration.title: stimulus duration
stimulus_duration.description: How long to display the stimulus in milliseconds. The visibility CSS property of the stimulus will be set to `hidden` after this time has elapsed. If this is null, then the stimulus will remain visible until the trial ends.

trial_duration.title: trial duration
trial_duration.description: ow long to wait for the participant to make a response before ending the trial in milliseconds. If the participant fails to make a response before this timer is reached, the participant's response will be recorded as null for the trial and the trial will end. If the value of this parameter is null, the trial will wait for a response indefinitely.

button_layout.title: button layout
button_layout.description: Setting to `'grid'` will make the container element have the CSS property `display: grid` and enable the use of `grid_rows` and `grid_columns`. Setting to `'flex'` will make the container element have the CSS property `display: flex`. You can customize how the buttons are laid out by adding inline CSS in the `button_html` parameter.

grid_rows.title: grid rows
grid_rows.description: The number of rows in the button grid. Only applicable when `button_layout` is set to `'grid'`. If null, the number of rows will be determined automatically based on the number of buttons and the number of columns.

grid_columns.title: grid columns
grid_columns.description: The number of columns in the button grid. Only applicable when `button_layout` is set to `'grid'`. If null, the number of columns will be determined automatically based on the number of buttons and the number of rows.

You can set this parameter to `false` to force the participant to view a stimulus for a fixed amount of time, even if they respond before the time is complete.

pages.title: pages
pages.description: Each element of the array is the content for a single page. Each page should be an HTML-formatted string.

key_forward.title: key forward
key_forward.description: This is the key that the participant can press in order to advance to the next page. This key should be specified as a string (e.g., `'a'`, `'ArrowLeft'`, `' '`, `'Enter'`).

key_backward.title: key backward
key_backward.description: This is the key that the participant can press to return to the previous page. This key should be specified as a string (e.g., `'a'`, `'ArrowLeft'`, `' '`, `'Enter'`).

allow_backward.title: allow backward
allow_backward.description: If true, the participant can return to previous pages of the instructions. If false, they may only advace to the next page.

allow_keys.title: allow keys
allow_keys.description: If `true`, the participant can use keyboard keys to navigate the pages. If `false`, they may not.

show_clickable_nav.title: show clickable nav
show_clickable_nav.description: If true, then a `Previous` and `Next` button will be displayed beneath the instructions. Participants can click the buttons to navigate.

show_page_number.title: show page number
show_page_number.description: If true, and clickable navigation is enabled, then Page x/y will be shown between the nav buttons.

page_label.title: page label
page_label.description: The text that appears before x/y pages displayed when show_page_number is true.

button_label_previous.title: button label previous
button_label_previous.description: The text that appears on the button to go backwards.

button_label_next.title: button label next
button_label_next.description: The text that appears on the button to go forwards.

on_page_change.title: Page change callback
on_page_change.description: The callback function when page changes

auto_preload.title: auto preload
auto_preload.description: If `true`, the plugin will preload any files that can be automatically preloaded based on the main experiment timeline that is passed to `jsPsych.run`. If `false`, any file(s) to be preloaded should be specified by passing a timeline array to the `trials` parameter and/or an array of file paths to the `images`, `audio`, and/or `video` parameters. Setting this parameter to `false` is useful when you plan to preload your files in smaller batches throughout the experiment.

trials.title: trials
trials.description: An array containing one or more jsPsych trial or timeline objects. This parameter is useful when you want to automatically preload stimuli files from a specific subset of the experiment. See [Creating an Experiment: The Timeline](../overview/timeline.md) for information on constructing timelines.

images.title: images
images.description: Array with one or more image files to load. This parameter is often used in cases where media files cannot be automatically preloaded based on the timeline, e.g. because the media files are passed into an image plugin/parameter with timeline variables or dynamic parameters, or because the image is embedded in an HTML string.

audio.title: audio
audio.description: Array with one or more audio files to load. This parameter is often used in cases where media files cannot be automatically preloaded based on the timeline, e.g. because the media files are passed into an audio plugin/parameter with timeline variables or dynamic parameters, or because the audio is embedded in an HTML string.

video.title: video
video.description: Array with one or more video files to load. This parameter is often used in cases where media files cannot be automatically preloaded based on the timeline, e.g. because the media files are passed into a video plugin/parameter with timeline variables or dynamic parameters, or because the video is embedded in an HTML string.

message.title: message
message.description: HTML-formatted message to show above the progress bar while the files are loading. If `null`, then no message is shown.

show_progress_bar.title: show progress bar
show_progress_bar.description: If `true`, a progress bar will be shown while the files are loading. If `false`, no progress bar is shown.

continue_after_error.title: continue after error
continue_after_error.description: Whether or not to continue with the experiment if a loading error occurs. If false, then if a loading error occurs, the error_message will be shown on the page and the trial will not end. If true, then if if a loading error occurs, the trial will end and preloading failure will be logged in the trial data.

error_message.title: error message
error_message.description: HTML-formatted message to be shown on the page after loading fails or times out. Only applies when `continue_after_error` is `false`.

show_detailed_errors.title: show detailed errors
show_detailed_errors.description: Whether or not to show a detailed error message on the page. If true, then detailed error messages will be shown on the page for all files that failed to load, along with the general error_message. This parameter is only relevant when continue_after_error is false.

max_load_time.title: max load time
max_load_time.description: The maximum amount of time that the plugin should wait before stopping the preload and either ending the trial (if continue_after_error is true) or stopping the experiment with an error message (if continue_after_error is false). If null, the plugin will wait indefintely for the files to load.

on_error.title: on error
on_error.description: Function to be called after a file fails to load. The function takes the file name as its only argument.

on_success.title: on success
on_success.description: Function to be called after a file loads successfully. The function takes the file name as its only argument.

stimuli.title: Stimuli
stimuli.description: The objects drawn on the canvas, each placed by its centre.

show_start_time.title: Show start time

show_end_time.title: Show end time
show_end_time.description: Time to end presenting the stimuli

show_start_frame.title: Show start frame
show_start_frame.description: Time to start presenting the stimuli in frames

show_end_frame.title: Show end frame
show_end_frame.description: Time to end presenting the stimuli in frames

lineJoin.title: lineJoin
lineJoin.description: The type of the corner when two lines meet.

drawFunc.title: Draw function
drawFunc.description: This function enables to move objects horizontally and vertically.

change_attr.title: Change attributes
change_attr.description: This function enables to change attributes of objects immediately before drawing.

is_frame.title: time is in frames
is_frame.description: If true, time is treated in frames.

prepared.title: Stimulus prepared flag
prepared.description: If true, the stimulus is prepared for presentation

origin_center.title: origin_center
origin_center.description: The origin is the center of the window.

is_presented.title: is_presented
is_presented.description: This will be true when the stimulus is presented.

trial_ends_after_audio.title: Trial ends after audio
trial_ends_after_audio.description: If true, then the trial will end as soon as the audio file finishes playing.

modulate_color.title: modulate_color
modulate_color.description: The base RGBA array of the gabor patch.

offset_color.title: offset_color
offset_color.description: The offset RGBA array of the gabor patch.

min_validModulationRange.title: min_validModulationRange
min_validModulationRange.description: The minimum of the validation range of the gabor patch.

max_validModulationRange.title: max_validModulationRange
max_validModulationRange.description: The maximum of the validation range of the gabor patch.

tilt.title: tilt
tilt.description: The angle of the gabor patch in degrees.

sf.title: spatial frequency
sf.description: The spatial frequency of the gabor patch.

phase.title: phase
phase.description: The phase (degrees) of the gabor patch.

sc.title: standard deviation
sc.description: The standard deviation of the distribution.

contrast.title: contrast
contrast.description: The contrast of the gabor patch.

drift.title: drift
drift.description: The velocity of the drifting gabor patch.

method.title: gabor_drawing_method
method.description: The method of drawing the gabor patch.

disableNorm.title: disableNorm
disableNorm.description: Disable normalization of the gaussian function.

disableGauss.title: disableGauss
disableGauss.description: Disable to convolve with a Gaussian.

questions.title: questions
questions.description: An array of objects, each object represents a question that appears on the screen. Each object contains a prompt, options, required, and horizontal parameter that will be applied to the question. See examples below for further clarification.`prompt`: Type string, default value is *undefined*. The string is prompt/question that will be associated with a group of options (radio buttons). All questions will get presented on the same page (trial). `options`: Type array, defualt value is *undefined*. An array of strings. The array contains a set of options to display for an individual question.`required`: Type boolean, default value is null. The boolean value indicates if a question is required('true') or not ('false'), using the HTML5 `required` attribute. If this parameter is undefined, the question will be optional. `horizontal`:Type boolean, default value is false. If true, then the question is centered and the options are displayed horizontally. `name`: Name of the question. Used for storing data. If left undefined then default names (`Q0`, `Q1`, `...`) will be used for the questions.

block.title: Runs its steps once per row of a conditions table.

conditions.title: The name of the conditions table this block runs over.

randomize_order.title: Shuffle the rows for every participant.

repetitions.title: How many times to go through the whole table.

children.title: The steps run for each row.

loop.title: Repeats its steps while a tagged set of trials stays below an accuracy threshold.

assign.title: Splits participants between groups: a between-subjects manipulation.

method.title: How a group is chosen.
method.description: `random` decides in the browser; `balanced` asks the data service for the next group, which requires uploading data with an experiment id.

record_as.title: Column name the chosen group is recorded under.

groups.title: The groups participants are split between.

counterbalance.title: Runs every task for every participant, in an order that varies between participants.

method.title: How each participant's order is chosen.
method.description: `random` shuffles the tasks in the browser; `latin_square` asks the data service for the participant's row of a balanced Latin square, which requires uploading data with an experiment id. With data downloaded, only `random` is available.

record_as.title: Column name the order used is recorded under, as "first > second".

tasks.title: The tasks whose order is counterbalanced.

branch.title: Sends a participant down one of two paths depending on how they did or what they answered.

then.title: Steps run when the rule holds.

otherwise.title: Steps run when it does not.

checkpoint.title: Records that a participant reached a point in the study, for drop-out analysis.

end.title: Ends the study here, the way one of the recruitment endings says, after saving the data.

ending.title: The name of an ending in `recruitment.endings`, such as `no_consent`.

variableReference.title: A value read from a column of the enclosing conditions table.

wrap.title: Markup the column's value is placed inside, with the value where `%s` is.

code.title: JavaScript the author wrote: the function itself for a parameter that takes one, or an expression worked out when the trial starts. `jsPsych` is in scope.

scoringRule.title: What counts as a correct response on this trial.

accuracyRule.title: A threshold applied to the trials carrying one tag.

scope.title: The tag whose trials are measured.

not.title: A rule compares accuracy one way, not both at once.

responseRule.title: Holds when the latest answer on the trials carrying one tag matches.

scope.title: The tag whose most recent trial is read.

response_equals.title: The answer looked for, compared as text: `1` matches the second button.

question.title: The question to read when a trial asks several, as a survey does.

experimentSettings.title: Settings that apply to the whole experiment rather than to one step.

default_iti.title: Gap in milliseconds after every trial, unless a step sets its own.

minimum_valid_rt.title: Responses faster than this are ignored, in milliseconds.

background_color.title: What the participant's screen looks like behind the stimulus.

save.title: `download` saves a CSV on the participant's machine, `post` uploads it.

experiment_id.title: The experiment id the endpoint files the data under.

then.title: Uploading needs an experiment id from the service receiving the data.

recruitmentSettings.title: How the study meets the platform participants are recruited from.

id_param.title: The URL parameter the platform passes the participant's id in.

endings.title: What happens when the study ends each way it can.
endings.description: `complete` is how the study ends once every step has run; any other ending is reached through an `end` step, such as `no_consent` for a participant who declines.

allOf.title: A completed study keeps all its data.

ending.title: Where the participant goes, or what they are shown, once their data is saved.

url.title: The platform's return URL; `{participant_id}` is replaced with the id.

message.title: Shown to the participant, who stays on the page, instead of a return URL.

keep.title: What is saved on reaching this ending.
keep.description: `all` saves every row, `checkpoint` only the row saying which ending was reached, and `nothing` saves and sends nothing at all. Only an early ending can keep less than `all`.

name.title: The name the spec refers to this file by, e.g. "face.png".

url.title: A data URL holding the file.
